## Message from the HOD

Image: Charles Obat

Welcome to Tom Mboya University Library, established in 2016 when the institution was founded. What began as a modest collection of books has grown into a vibrant academic resource center with over thirteen thousand processed volumes actively utilized by our community.

Our comprehensive collection spans diverse disciplines including Linguistics, Biological Sciences, Physical Sciences, Business, Humanities, and more. Through our subscription to KLISC, we provide access to an extensive range of electronic resources.

The library takes pride in its team of qualified and dedicated professionals committed to delivering exceptional service to both students and faculty members.

## Message from the Head of Department

Image: Charles Obat

Welcome to Tom Mboya University Library, established in 2016 when the institution was founded. What began as a modest collection of books has grown into a vibrant academic resource center with over thirteen thousand processed volumes actively utilized by our community.

Our comprehensive collection spans diverse disciplines including Linguistics, Biological Sciences, Physical Sciences, Business, Humanities, and more. Through our subscription to the Kenya Libraries and Information Services Consortium (KLISC), we provide access to an extensive range of electronic resources to support your academic journey.

The library takes pride in its team of qualified and dedicated professionals committed to delivering exceptional service to both students and faculty members. We continuously enhance our offerings to meet the evolving needs of our academic community.

The Library Department warmly welcomes you to Tom Mboya University.

Charles Obat

Head of Library Department

# Library Catalogue (OPAC)

Search our physical collection of books and information resources

### What is OPAC?

The Online Public Access Catalog enables you to search the entire physical collection at Tom Mboya University Library — books, journals, theses and more.

### How to Use

  * Enter keywords, author, title or subject in the search box
  * Browse results and note call numbers
  * Visit the library to borrow physical copies

### Search Tips

  * Use specific keywords for better results
  * Try different combinations of search terms
  * Use quotation marks for exact phrases
  * Filter by publication year when available
